title: Make Lookup
prompt: A TypeScript feature flag system wants lookup by key. Write a function that turns an array of entries into an object where each key maps to its enabled boolean.

explanation.beginner:
Example: makeLookup([{"key":"beta","enabled":true},{"key":"ads","enabled":false}]) produces {"beta":true,"ads":false}. Associate each record with its stable ID. Each assignment updates one lookup entry; duplicate IDs follow the stated overwrite rule.

Compare “handles empty arrays”: input [[]] produces {}. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Associate each record with its stable ID. Each assignment updates one lookup entry; duplicate IDs follow the stated overwrite rule.

Tempting mistake: Array positions are not stable identifiers after sorting or filtering. Repeated IDs require an explicit first-wins or last-wins policy.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “handles empty arrays”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
